item.title: NFL injury tracker Week 6: Latest news, fantasy implications as Caleb Williams (hamstring) returns to practice, Lamar Jackson (ankle) remains out, injuries pile up for Eagles
item.description: Everything you need to know injury-wise for Week 6 of the NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
Week 6 is underway, and we're tracking all the injuries before game time.

Is this the week that both Caleb Williams and Lamar Jackson return to action? It's looking more likely for one quarterback than the other.

Williams returned to practice this week with the Chicago Bears as a full participant. He also informed the media that he was dealing with a torn hamstring, not a Grade 2 injury as was originally reported. The quarterback has missed three games since suffering the injury at the end of their Week 2 defeat to the Minnesota Vikings.

Before he can return to face the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, Williams said he needed to undergo stress tests to assess where he's at before being declared good to go.

Meanwhile, Lamar Jackson remains out of practice as the Baltimore Ravens signal-caller continues to deal with an ankle injury.

After sitting out Week 5, Jackson's status for the matchup against the Cleveland Browns is in doubt. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter labeled the quarterback day-to-day and said, "He's doing everything he can to be out here, and when he's able to be, then he will."

Tyler Huntley would get his second straight start should Jackson be ruled out for another week.

The injuries continue in Philadelphia with quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clot) and running back Will Shipley (foot) already set to miss Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.

Wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), who has missed the past two games, was limited in practice on Thursday, while running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring), who sat out last week, remained out. It could be a week where Dameon Pierce is the featured back for the Eagles.

Other Week 6 injuries to monitor

  • It was reported that New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was set to miss "multiple" weeks. But there he was on Thursday taking part in practice as a limited participant for a second straight day trying to give himself a chance to play Sunday against the New York Jets.

  • The 21-day practice window was opened this week for A.J. Brown (ankle), who has been out since Week 1. The Patriots wide receiver said it's "still up in the air" if he plays this week. The team has three weeks to activate him off injured reserve and return him to the 53-man roster.

  • Running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is in danger of missing Week 6 for the Cleveland Browns. Judkins suffered the injury against the Jets last week and was spotted in a walking boot earlier this week. Head coach Todd Monken said Judkins was day-to-day and the walking boot was just a precaution.

  • Rashee Rice (hamstring) missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday with what Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid called a "tweak." The wide receiver picked up the injury early in the team's Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

item.description: The Darius Slayton experiment in Indianapolis has come to an end.
item.content:encoded:
The Darius Slayton experiment in Indianapolis has come to an end.

The Colts announced on Friday that the team has released Slayton, ending the veteran wideout’s short stint with the club.

Indianapolis had signed Slayton after Alec Pierce went down early in the season with the hope that he could fill in as a deep threat.

But nearly a month later, Slatyon had yet to see the field. Now, the Colts have moved on.

Last season, Slayton caught 37 passes for 538 yards with one touchdown in 14 games for the Giants last year.

item.title: Which Week 6 game are you most looking forward to?
item.description: Which Week 6 game are you most looking forward to watching?
item.content:encoded:
After a nice bounce-back performance in the desert in Week 5, where the Detroit Lions rolled over the Arizona Cardinals to the tune of 45-21, the team now heads into their bye week on a high note. And while having a Week 6 bye isn’t the most ideal in terms of where it falls during the course of the regular season, it comes at a decent time for Detroit. They are 3-2 through five weeks of play, firmly in contention in what figures to be a highly competitive NFC North race, and will likely be getting some reinforcements after the bye week is over.

Now with the players enjoying their bye week and most of the coaches likely hunkered down at 222 Republic Drive preparing for the Week 7 matchup against the Green Bay Packers, we get to enjoy a weekend of stress-free football. That brings us to today’s question of the day—which game from the Week 6 slate are you most looking forward to watching?

My answer: Naturally, I am going with the Sunday Night Football game between the Packers and the Dallas Cowboys. Green Bay has had some major ups-and-downs so far this year, while the Cowboys feature one of the more high-powered offenses in the game. Could this be a primetime shootout at Lambeau Field? Either way, it will be a chance for Lions fans to get one last look at the Packers before Week 7 rolls around.

What about you? Which game from the Week 6 slate are you most looking forward to watching? Let us know in the comments below.

item.title: Questions ahead of Mizzou’s top-15 matchup in Oxford
item.description: Injuries, a potential return at edge rusher, and a tough QB matchup, what questions remain heading into Saturday?
item.content:encoded:
Ahead of No. 13 Mizzou’s matchup with No. 9 Mississippi, there are plenty of intriguing questions surrounding a top-15 matchup in Oxford.

Thursday night’s injury report heading into Saturday will likely elevate some players to bigger roles, while one is expected to make his full return. Meanwhile, defensively, the Tigers are going against their toughest quarterback yet on the road, three weeks after playing Kamario Taylor.

The game is right around the corner, and there are still a few things worth talking about ahead of Saturday. Here are four questions for Mizzou as it takes on Mississippi.

With Brett Norfleet doubtful, what’s next for the tight end room?

Let’s be honest, Mizzou’s tight end room hasn’t received the opportunities and production that was anticipated headed into this season. When targeted in the passing game, Brett Norfleet accounts for 14 of the room’s 15 targets. The other going to Jordon Harris. 

On Thursday night, per Pete Thamel of ESPN, among the most significant changes on the Tigers’ injury report was Norfleet being downgraded from questionable to doubtful ahead of Saturday.

And with Gavin Hoffman out as well, if Norfleet doesn’t suit up, it would just leave Harris and Jude James as remaining options in terms of players who have received playing time in the room. Harris is predominantly a run blocker, with 200 of his 223 offensive snaps coming this season being in pass or run blocking situations, while James has been on the field for just 69 offensive snaps. 

If Mizzou is going to target the tight ends at all in the passing game, both Harris and James are going to have to step up in big ways. James will likely be asked to take on Nofleet’s run-blocking snaps as well. 

But against Ole Miss, it presents an opportunity for the tight end room to thrive. In four of the Rebel’s five games this season, an opposing tight end has gone for over 30 yards receiving. That may not seem like much, but the last MU tight end to do that was Oct. 11, 2025, against Alabama.

The opportunities will be there for Harris and James if Norfleet is out, but it’s an interesting situation to watch for on Saturday.

And with Jeremiah Beasley being designated the same status as Norfleet, who is up next?

Linebacker Jeremiah Beasley is also doubtful for Saturday afternoon and Robert Woodyard Jr. is questionable. In terms of usage so far this season, he’s 19th in the team’s defensive snaps (110), which ranks third in the linebacker room. He saw an uptick in snaps against Florida (30) with both Robert Woodyard Jr. and Nicholas Rodriguez battling injury, and saw 11 snaps vs. Texas A&M.

So, who will be up next to play alongside Woodyard, Rodriguez, and Chris McClellan?

On Week 7’s depth chart, Brian Huff was listed as the alternate alongside Beasley. He’s played just three snaps in SEC play, but Bobby Washington Jr. also played six snaps against A&M, and specifically was used as a QB spy per Eli Drinkwitz postgame. Washington could be used in that same role, but if Beasley can’t go, the Tigers will be reaching deeper into their depth to fill the void.

What difference could Darris Smith in a return?

Darris Smith tried to give it a go against Texas A&M, but wasn’t quite ready, playing just five snaps. His status for Saturday is upgraded to probable, signaling his return in Oxford. 

The last time we saw Smith in a full game came in Lawrence against Kansas, and he was extremely effective, generating eight pressures. Mizzou was credited with 40 on the night, per PFF. Since then, Mizzou’s pressure total as a team has been 12, 8, 17, and 17. But, for the first time since Week 2, the Tigers are trending towards having their full pass rush arsenal back of Smith, Langden Kitchen, and Daeden Hopkins. 

Mizzou is going up against a quarterback, whose statistics alter when pressured. Per PFF, Trinidad Chambliss has an adjusted completion percentage of just 58.8%, compared to 76.5 when kept clean. This ranks 10th among SEC quarterbacks. Getting pressure on Chambliss is a must and having Smith back is a step forward to that.

Speaking of Chambliss, how will Mizzou’s defense hold up against this style of QB?

Mizzou has played an interesting slate of quarterbacks so far this season, but with Chambliss trending towards a first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, this will be the toughest quarterback the Tigers will play so far this season.

The last time the Tigers played on the road against Mississippi State, Taylor put stress on the entire defense. Chambliss can do the exact same thing, arguably better. He possesses the ability to attack every level of the field, but also has nine completions of 20-plus yards, seven big-time throws in that range.

“He’s able to extend plays, he’s got a really quick release, he see’s the field really well and throws with anticipations,” Drinkwitz said. “All those things are hallmarks of a good quarterback.”

 Fortunately, Mizzou’s defense has taken steps forward the past few weeks. From Matthew Gustafson’s Tiger Talk Notes and Quotes: Ole Miss Edition

(Eli Drinkwitz)On the defensive improvement over the past two weeks:“Those guys are playing really, really hard, very physical in the trenches and tackling really well, which I think is the hallmark of a really good defense. I’ve been impressed with these these past two games. This game’s a whole new challenge; it’s a totally different challenge with the quarterback, the running back, wide receiver, and the tempo. So we have to transition from patting ourselves in the back to getting our cleats in the ground and getting set and making sure we’re ready to go.”

Now, they will play a quarterback that can generate explosive plays, . The results weren’t great the first time, but they’ll get another chance to stop one of college football’s best quarterbacks.

item.title: Indianapolis Colts cut wide receiver Darius Slayton
item.description: We hardly knew ye.
item.content:encoded:
In what now seems like a very odd series of event the Indianapolis Colts have released Darius Slayton.

Slayton was signed on September 22nd following Alec Pierce’s week two injury that sent him to injured reserve. There was some hope that Slayton could come in and become a downfield option that the Colts lacked with Pierce out. In the end the Colts move on from Slayton without him ever appearing in a single game for the horseshoe.

Slayton was never going to be a revelation for a receiver corps struggling to produce week in and week out but at this point any veteran help they could get was being welcomed. Afterall, get a guy into a game and you never know, it’s possible he could have a game or make even a single play that could get Indy a win they otherwise wouldn’t have gotten. Instead the Colts move on and this brief signing will be nothing more than an answer to a weird Colts trivia question a decade from now.

The question now becomes, how do they fill this roster spot? It seems that tight end Will Mallory is close to making his return and while most probably would not love the move Anthony Gould keeps bouncing between the practice squad and being elevated for gameday, so that move could make some sense. What is unlikely is that there is any sort of needle moving transaction coming for the Indianapolis Colts, at least not until the offseason.

Check back in to see who fills out the 53.

item.title: Andrew Whitworth irritated with Harrison Mevis after Rams’ loss
item.description: Andrew Whitworth didn’t like how Harrison Mevis reacted after the latest Los Angeles Rams loss and more NFL news
item.content:encoded:
Andrew Whitworth explained on Fitz and Whit that he was a bit salty with Harrison Mevis after the Los Angeles Rams lost to the Buffalo Bills, and it wasn’t only because Mevis missed crucial kicks. It was because Mevis was laughing with Bills players after the loss.

Whitworth said that laughing after a loss doesn’t line up with what the Rams feel as a team, and it doesn’t line up with head coach Sean McVay. Odds are that Mevis would’ve been released after that game regardless of how Mevis acted, but Whitworth alludes it may have been a nail in the coffin for Mevis with the Rams.

Whitworth could be speaking for himself; he could be speaking for some players and coaches on the team. It’s an interesting take by “Big Whit”.

The end of a football game is an emotional time typically for both teams as one is elated from their victory, the other gutted from a loss, or it’s a tie in which case no one knows how to feel. Players handle those reactions differently.

When players laugh after a loss, I see both sides. On the one hand you lost, what’s funny? On the other hand, these guys are playing in some cases their brothers, best friends, family, college teammates, high school teammates and longtime rivals. I can understand how a player can be gutted from a loss, but still excited to see someone they care about.

I don’t disagree with what Whit is saying because it’s his opinion. What I will say is whether Mevis was laughing or not after the loss if he was the best kicker in the league, he’d still be on the team.

Mevis wasn’t the best kicker in the league, and his laughing after a loss didn’t help his case with the Rams. It will be interesting to see if Mevis gets another shot elsewhere.

Andrew Whitworth calls out Harrison Mevis for laughing after Rams’ loss (ramswire)

“The identity and the mentality of football teams that are really good usually match up. Like, when you go look at the teams that lose a lot, I can show you a lot of guys that don’t always show they care the most. But like, if you are in the mood to go laugh and keekee with some Bills players after the game, you don’t match up to the head coach’s mentality because I know that dude. Like, the whole world stops when he doesn’t perform. When Matthew Stafford, at this point in his career, what he’s trying to accomplish, what Davante Adams wants, what Aaron Donald came back for, right? Like, there is no answer other than winning. You see, Mevis gets released. It’s exactly what I’m saying. There’s an identity and mentality to our football team.”

LA Rams EDGE Myles Garrett will not return in Week 6 vs. Arizona Cardinals (cardswire)

“The Arizona Cardinals will face the Los Angeles Rams, but they do get a little bit of a break. Pass rusher Myles Garrett will not return this week.

Garrett, on injured reserve with a knee injury, was eligible to have his practice window opened this week. That didn’t happen. Head coach Sean McVay told reporters Tuesday that Garrett would not practice this week.

He could potentially in Week 7, but the Cardinals will miss him.

However, while Garrett won’t play, the Cardinals will still have to face pass rusher Byron Young, who leads the Rams with 3.5 sacks through five games.“

McVay faces former offensive coordinator LaFleur for first time when Rams host Cardinals (pinalcentral)

“The Rams (2-3) are trying to get on track after an erratic start to the season, while the Cardinals (1-4) are seeking to recapture the success of their surprising season-opening visit to SoFi Stadium, when they knocked off the building’s other tenant, the Chargers. In short, there is a lot more for both sides to worry about rather than friendships and returning to one’s former place of employment.

“As much as I love Sean, I haven’t really thought of him too much,” LaFleur said. “I’m sure he’s kind of feeling the same way about me right now.”

Rams Midweek Report: Favorable Schedule Ahead, Myles Garrett Update, Sean McVay Concerns (si.com)

“Given the issues on special teams, it’s hard to put a lot of faith in this team. They continuously invent new ways to lose. For the first time this season, the Rams are no longer Super Bowl favorites as that belongs to the San Francisco 49ers. 

At the same time, if the Rams can figure it out, there is the potential for them to go on a serious run. Here is their schedule before the bye week in Week 11: 

  • Week 6 vs. Arizona Cardinals 1-4
  • Week 7 @ Las Vegas Raiders 3-2
  • Week 8 vs. Los Angeles Chargers 0-5
  • Week 9 @ Washington Commanders 1-3-1
  • Week 10 @ Arizona Cardinals 1-4

The combined record for those teams is 6-18-1. That’s the lowest strength of schedule over the next five games in the NFL.It’s important not to look too far ahead in the NFL, but those are five very winnable games. The Rams could easily go into their bye week with a 7-3 record. At that point, the Rams may only be one or two games back in the NFC West behind the 49ers.“ 

Arizona Cardinals vs Los Angeles Rams Betting Preview: Week 6 Odds, Tips and Prediction (compare.bet)

“Twelve and a half points is the biggest handicap on the Week 6 board, and it is being laid by a team with a losing record. The Rams are 2-3. Their point difference is minus one.

The case for the number is that the matchup is brutal. Los Angeles lead the NFL in passing at 310.4 yards a game and are second in passing yards allowed at 163.4. They throw it better than anyone and stop it better than almost anyone. Arizona concede 32.4 points a game, the most in the league.“

Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams, Aaron Donald & Puka Nacua preview Week 6 vs. the Cardinals (therams.com)

“Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay, quarterback Matthew Stafford, wide receivers Davante Adams & Puka Nacua, and defensive end Aaron Donald speak with the media on Thursday. Watch them reflect on lessons from Monday’s matchup vs. the Buffalo Bills, preview Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals, and more.”

Matthew Stafford reveals the Rams’ biggest problem — and it’s not the kicker (nypost)

“The problem isn’t necessarily how the Rams finish games or what the offense does when its backs are against the wall and it needs a score. They’ve been excellent when urgency is required, especially in two-minute situations. It’s more about the opportunities they miss before they reach the finish line.

“There’s chances all over the place in games to snatch the momentum, or go pile on a lead, or claw back a little closer, so it’s not just about one possession at the end of the game, or whatever that is,” Stafford said.

Over their last three games, the Rams have mastered the art of playing with their backs against the wall. Now they need to figure out how to play with that same sense of desperation before their opponent puts it there.“

Best Los Angeles Rams fantasy performances so far this season (keyt.com)

“Every season in the NFL produces performances that feel less like a single game and more like statistical outliers — explosive outings where quarterbacks pile up passing yards, running backs break off long scoring runs, and receivers turn routine targets into multi-touchdown afternoons. These are the kinds of games that separate good fantasy weeks from historic ones.

Stacker compiled a ranking of the best Los Angeles Rams fantasy performances in the 2026 season using data from Stathead. The list includes the highest single-game fantasy scores by quarterbacks, running backs, wide receivers, and tight ends. Players are ranked based on standard fantasy scoring.“

Matthew Stafford steady in high-pressure moments over last three weeks (rams.com)

“”You expect somebody to be more frantic in some of those situations than what he is,” wide receiver Davante Adams said on Thursday of Stafford’s demeanor during two-minute drills. “I always allude to the fact that he’s the coolest and most collected guy that I’ve been around. Period. But just the way he commands the huddle in some of those moments is special. And I think that we get a lot of our confidence from him just based off that he seems and feels in the moment. So (we) just kind of follow that.”

The way the Rams quarterback conducts himself in the huddle and on the field in late-game situations with everything on the line sets the tone for the rest of the offense. And on Monday night against the Bills, Stafford excelled in those moments with the highest pressure.“

Rams vs. Cardinals Week 6 Prediction: Preview, Matchups, and Players to Watch (si.com)

“The Cardinals have typically provided the Rams a ‘get right’ opportunity in past seasons. After losing two straight last year, the Rams beat the Cardinals in Week 18 before going into the playoffs. It was what the Rams needed to feel good heading into the postseason. Following the loss to the Bills, the Rams need that more than ever. 

Rams Offense vs. Cardinals Defense

Heading into Sunday, the Rams will be without left tackle Alaric Jackson as he serves a suspension from the NFL following an incident after the Bills’ game. That will leave the Rams with David Quessenberry at left tackle. The last time the Rams were without Jackson against the Cardinals, they lost, 41-10, and Dennis Gardeck had three sacks. The Cardinals have generated pressure on just 30.3 percent of dropbacks this season, which is the second-lowest rate in the NFL. “

item.description: The Patriots are entering Sunday’s game as favorites over the Jets.
item.content:encoded:
Winners of two straight games, the New England Patriots will be looking to add a third victory to their current streak to improve to 4-2 on the season. Standing between them is a division foe, a New York Jets team coming off a victory in Week 5 itself.

According to FanDuel Sportsbook, the Patriots are seen as 7.5-point favorites at home. Will they prove the oddsmakers right? Or will the Jets manage to pull off a big upset at Gillette Stadium? Let’s find out what Pats Pulpit’s staff and community think.

Patriots vs. Jets score predictions

Bernd Buchmasser: Much like the Patriots earlier in the year, the Jets are still finding themselves offensively. The problem for them is that doing so against a New England defense that should get Christian Gonzalez back will be a tall task — too tall a task. With New York’s offense not exactly threatening and Drake Maye and company having started to find their groove, this has the makings of a “rest the starters in the fourth quarter to get them ready for Thursday”-type of game. | Patriots 31, Jets 13

Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle!

Follow every snap and discuss every decision with fellow fans on the SB Nation app.

  • Connect through our live game chat
  • Browse with fewer ads
  • Seamlessly move between communities
  • Enjoy faster commenting and posting

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android.

Matt St. Jean: The Patriots dominated the Jets twice last season, and with some reinforcements on their way I expect Mike Vrabel’s squad to pick up where they left off last December. This Jets group is clearly improved from last year’s version, but not at the level to make this game competitive. | Patriots 38, Jets 13

Dylan Klayman: The Jets have looked like they are on an upwards trajectory from the abysmal state that they were in last season. Coming off a win against the Browns, who are having a resurgence of their own, the Jets have a talented defense with a very high blitz rate. However, with Drake Maye and the Patriots’ offense looking like they are back to their 2025 form over the past two games, and their defense playing at such a high level, they should defeat this Jets team comfortably. | Patriots 31, Jets 10

Pat Lane: The Jets are better than they were, but they still stink. The Patriots seem to have righted the ship, and now are getting some players back too. This shouldn’t be close. I know the Jets defense is aggressive, but Josh McDaniels should be able to use that against them. Garrett Wilson is one of the best receivers in the league against man coverage, but getting Christian Gonzalez back shouldn’t make that a problem. The Patriots roll and get ready for a quick turnaround with Thursday Night Football in Chicago on the horizon. | Patriots 34, Jets 14

Andrew Guindon: The Jets are better than they were last season; however, the Patriots should handily advance to 4-2. New York’s defensive line could create issues for New England offensively, but even though that unit already has 17 sacks on the year, they don’t generate pressure consistently. The Jets also don’t have the offense to match the Patriots, especially if a healthy Christian Gonzalez shadows Garrett Wilson. | Patriots 34, Jets 10

What do you think? Do you agree with our assessment? Or do you feel differently one way or the other? Please head down to the comment section to share your thoughts with the rest of the community.

item.title: Dallas Cowboys offensive line vs. Green Bay Packers defense
item.description: The Cowboys offensive line needs to have a big game on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys need a get-right game against the Green Bay Packers. One of the biggest keys to making that happen is the work of the offensive line. Let’s see how they match up with the Packers.

Trench Dashboard

Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far. 

Pass Block Win Rate – 50% (17th)

Run Block Win Rate – 69% (31st)

Pressure rate allowed – 27% (10th)

Sacks allowed – 6 (2nd)

Last three-week trend: Pass protection steady, run blocking fading

The pressure point

Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for.

PRESSURE POINT: Green Bay’s blitzes are more dangerous than its four-man rush

There is an unusual split in Green Bay’s defensive numbers. The Packers have 14 sacks, seventh-most in the NFL, yet their Passs Rush Win Rate ranks 29th (see below). 

That tells us Green Bay is not consistently dominating offensive linemen one-on-one. Instead, defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has been willing to create pressure with extra rushers and disguise. Through the first four games, Green Bay has blitzed a healthy amount, something to expect this week against Dallas. 

That matters after what happened against Tampa Bay. The Buccaneers repeatedly confused Dallas with blitzes and different pressure looks. Dak Prescott was officially sacked zero times, but the offense struggled to consistently identify where pressure was coming from and never developed a comfortable rhythm. Tampa Bay controlled possession for more than 39 minutes and Dallas produced only 16 points.

That means Cooper Beebe has to identify those looks before the snap. Tyler Smith and Tyler Booker also have to communicate when defenders cross over each other or linebackers arrive late. Dallas protected Prescott well statistically against Tampa Bay. The next step is protecting him without the offense becoming uncomfortable every time a defense threatens to blitz.

PRESSURE POINT: Devonte Wyatt is now the main interior threat

Micah Parsons was hoping to return against his former team, but Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur said the Packers are still waiting for medical clearance, and Parsons is not expected to return this week. That removes the biggest possible matchup nightmare from Dallas’ preparation. But Devonte Wyatt cannot be ignored.

Wyatt produced two sacks against Chicago last week, giving Green Bay an explosive interior pass-rush option. Interior pressure can be particularly damaging because Prescott cannot simply step forward away from an edge rusher. If Wyatt gets through the middle, the pocket disappears directly in front of the quarterback.

Where to attack

Every defensive line has a weakness, here are the Packers soft spots where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. 

GREEN LIGHT: Run directly at Green Bay’s depleted middle

Green Bay’s 27% Run Stop Win Rate ranks 28th in the NFL. Opponents have already rushed for 638 yards and eight touchdowns at 4.1 yards per carry. The Packers have also suffered two enormous injury losses.

Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper is out for the season after tearing his Achilles, that’s a huge loss. Cooper had 30 tackles and six tackles for loss before the injury and was becoming one of Green Bay’s most important defensive players. 

Then defensive tackle Javon Hargrave suffered an Achilles injury against Chicago and is also expected to miss the remainder of the season. That is exactly where Dallas needs to attack.

Booker’s 80.0 PFF run-blocking grade ranks ninth among guards, while Smith gives Dallas its most powerful offensive lineman back on the opposite side. Dallas should use double teams inside and make Green Bay’s replacement linebackers come downhill to make tackles.

GREEN LIGHT: Make Green Bay prove it can win with four rushers

The Packers’ sack total looks intimidating, but there’s a way to show these numbers are wonky. Green Bay’s poor Pass Rush Win Rate combined with an equally bad 25% in defensive pressure rate that ranks 24th in the league, means their blitz game is how they generate sacks. 

If Green Bay only sends four defenders, it’s safe to say Dak can trust the offensive line. Tyler Guyton has been one of the biggest positives of the Cowboys season. Among tackles in the league he’s near the top in most statistical categories and PFF blocking grades. 

If Guyton and Terence Steele can hold up against Green Bay’s edge rushers, Dallas can release Jake Ferguson and the running backs into routes instead of constantly keeping extra blockers beside the tackles. If Green Bay responds by blitzing, Prescott needs immediate answers and everything boils down to the interior.

The Chaos Report

Here’s the Green Bay Packers defensive trends for this season at the defensive line.

Sack Total – 14 (7th)

Pass Rush Win Rate – 43% (29th)

Run Stop Win Rate – 27% (28th)

QB Pressure Rate – 25% (24th)

Last three-week trend: Sacks climbing, injuries mounting 

Matchup of the week

Tyler Booker vs. Devonte Wyatt

For the first time in a few weeks, the key matchup is inside rather than at offensive tackle. Wyatt showed why against Chicago. He finished with two sacks and a forced fumble, creating pressure directly through the middle of the Bears offensive line. Booker is the Cowboy best equipped to stop him.

Dallas’ second-year guard has become arguably its most dependable run blocker. His PFF blocking grades rank highly among guards, and he has surrendered only six total pressures without allowing a sack this season. This matchup matters in both directions. When Dallas throws, Booker has to stop Wyatt from collapsing the pocket into Prescott.

When Dallas runs, Booker needs to move Wyatt backwards and create space for Javonte Williams. With Hargrave unavailable, Green Bay has lost one of the players who could rotate inside and keep its defensive tackles fresh. That gives Dallas another reason to keep pounding away.

Best route to success: 

Make Green Bay stop the run before worrying about its blitzes. Dallas rushed for only 50 yards last week and now ranks 29th in the league in rushing production and 31st in Run Block Win Rate.

However, Green Bay ranks 28th in Run Stop Win Rate. The Packers have lost Cooper and Hargrave, and Parsons is not expected to return, all this is major this week. 

Dallas needs to attack the middle, stay ahead of the chains and prevent Green Bay from reaching the situations where the Packers can unleash its pressure packages. If the Cowboys are constantly facing second-and-five and third-and-two, the Packers have to respect everything and defend the entirety of the Cowboys offense. 

Injury updates:

The Cowboys offensive line is at full strength. 

Green Bay has much bigger problems and are dangerously thin on the defensive line. 

With the names already mentioned, Jordon Riley is slowly returning from an Achilles injury he sustained in Week 17 of last season, so watch his name. Colin Oliver and Warren Brinson have both gone to IR, and Anthony Campbell is questionable so watch for his name on the practice report as well.

item.title: Steelers-Buccaneers preview: What to expect from Tampa Bay’s offense, defense in Week 6
item.description: Both teams are coming off encouraging Week 5 wins.
item.content:encoded:
The 3-2 Steelers will travel to Tampa Bay in Week 6 to take on the Buccaneers, who sit at a disappointing 1-4 but are coming off their lone win of the season thus far — a 24-16 showing against the Cowboys in Week 5.

It’s been a rough season for Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles and co., and the team’s recent three-year, $165 million extension for quarterback Baker Mayfield already isn’t aging that well: The veteran passer struggled in a winless start to the year before missing games with a dislocated thumb on this throwing hand.

But coming off a Thursday Night Football win in Dallas, the Buccaneers have some momentum and extra prep time to prepare for the Steelers. What should Pittsburgh expect on Sunday?

What to expect from the Bucs’ offense

Rushing YPG: 133 (7th)

Passing YPG: 173.4 (27th)

PPG: 20 (25th)

RB: The Buccaneers offense will be without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for yet another game, meaning undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will once again start under center for Tampa Bay against Pittsburgh.

The good news is that Daniels is a rookie with just two starts under his belt. That can show in his play and the Steelers should be able to take advantage of some mistakes on Sunday. That said, Mayfield was having a rough start to 2026, and it was Daniels who helped lead the Buccaneers to their first win of the season last week. Like everything in the NFL, beating the Buccaneers won’t be slam dunk in Week 6.

Daniels looked impressively poised and accurate against the Cowboys defense last week, passing for 189 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions with 76% completion. Of course, offensive coordinator Zac Robinson put together a game plan to help the young passer succeed, with an emphasis on the quick game and play action.

Daniels is on the shorter side for an NFL passer (6’0), and his arm strength doesn’t leap off the screen, but he drives the ball well on short and intermediate passes and only had a few rough misses against the Cowboys (note this was against a struggling Dallas defense). His escapability is an upgrade over Mayfield’s, with Daniels already having 87 yards and four first downs on the ground this season.

While the Buccaneers are largely a short-game passing attack, Daniels still has moments where his processing slows down and he attempts to play hero ball. Tampa Bay has a strong offensive line but currently has the third-worst sack rate in the NFL (10.1%), with 17 sacks allowed this season. A number of those plays have been quarterback error — Tampa Bay has the NFL’s seventh-longest time to throw at 2.98 seconds — even if Daniels has been an improvement in that area over Mayfield.

If the Steelers can keep up with Daniels in the backfield, they should be able to log some sacks or at least a handful of pressures on Sunday. But Tampa Bay’s offensive line won’t make that task easy.

Led by one of the league’s best tackles in Tristian Wirfs and a slew of other good players such as Graham Barton and Luke Goedeke, the Buccaneers can both pass protect well and maul in the run game.

On the ground, the Tampa holds defenses to the sixth-lowest run stuff rate (12.5%) in the NFL. The Buccaneers are also second-best in yards before contact per attempt (2.16), per NFL Pro.

The Buccaneers use a lot of motion to try to confuse defenses pre-snap, and it melds well with a rushing offense that favors gap concepts. At running back, the room has two solid names in starter Bucky Irving and former Steeler Kenny Gainwell. Both are slimmer running backs who can be a weapon in the passing game, with Irving showing off his phone-booth quickness with a long run against Dallas last week.

If healthy, Sean Tucker is another name to keep an eye on in Tampa Bay’s backfield as a more hard-nosed, downhill runner.

At pass catcher, the Buccaneers have a number of recognizable names, but still lack an established WR1. Emeka Egbuka leads the team in receiving yards with 192 through five games, averaging just 9.1 yards per reception as a primarily underneath target. Tight end Cade Otton, with 182 yards, has also been a steady contributor.

Chris Godwin Jr. hasn’t had his pre-injury production, but has been another solid name in the short game with 129 of his 179 yards this season coming after the catch. On more downfield passes, 5’10 speed threat Tez Johnson averages 27.6 yards per catch on five receptions this season, while rookie Ted Hurst III, one of my favorite mid-round prospects this spring, has made some plays with eight grabs for 128 yards and a touchdown this season.

Tampa Bay is one of the most 11 personnel-heavy offenses in the league, getting a wide range of receivers involved. Still, its running game ranks top 10 thanks to a competent offensive line.

On paper, the Steelers’ defense certainly has the talent to shut down the Buccaneers’ offense, but Daniels is a bit of an X factor. Will an experienced pass rush with more film on the rookie dominate, or will Daniels continue to improve and clean up Tampa Bay’s sack rate with his mobility? Also complicating things is the tendency for offensive coordinators to mix up their tendencies more when playing with a reserve quarterback.

However, if the Steelers can disrupt the Buccaneers’ quick passing game and run game and force Daniels to play out of rhythm and with more downfield shots, this game could bode well for the Pittsburgh defense.

What to expect from the Bucs’ defense

Rushing YPG Allowed: 72.8 (2nd)

Passing YPG Allowed: 226.6 (20th)

PPG Allowed: 22.4 (T-14th)

RP: The Buccaneers’ defense makes a fascinating matchup for the Steelers’ offense. This contest will pit strength against strength: Pittsburgh’s running game versus Tampa Bay’s run defense. But it will also feature weakness against weakness: the Steelers have struggled against man coverage, yet the Buccaneers run man concepts at a bottom-third rate in the league.

In most metrics, the Buccaneers’ run defense is near the top of the league, and their overall strategy is pretty apparent. Tampa Bay has light boxes — six or fewer defenders — at the second-lowest rate (20.7%) in the NFL. They have stacked boxes — eight or more defenders — at the second-highest rate (41.4%) in the league. Put another way, 79.3% of the time, the Bucs have seven defenders or more in the box against the run, giving them a numbers advantage if the offense doesn’t answer with some combination of two tight ends, a fullback, or a condensed formation that hugs the receivers tight to their linemen.

The results have followed. Not only are the Buccaneers allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game, but they’re also top-seven or better in:

  • Average yards after contact (1.72, 1st)
  • Yards per carry (3.3, T-2nd)
  • EPA/Rush (-0.18, 4th)
  • Runs of 10+ yards allowed (9, T-4th)
  • Run stuff rate (18.9%, 7th)

While he doesn’t fill up the stat sheet, plenty of credit for the Buccaneers’ success against the run should be paid to nose tackle Vita Vea.

The Bucs also find creative ways to get their linebackers and defensive backs in good position to make stops.

Safety Tykee Smith and rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter currently lead the team in run stuffs with four apiece.

Tampa Bay’s commitment to stopping the run bleeds into what coverages they run. They live in single-high safety looks, running Cover-1 (12.9%) and Cover-3 (51.7%) a combined 64.6% of the time.

Against the pass, Tampa is a mostly middling group. As a pass rush unit, they actually track well at creating pressure, but they struggle to pay it off. The Bucs have the second-quickest average time to create pressure (2.45 seconds), and opposing quarterbacks’ average time to throw (2.59 seconds) is the quickest mark in the NFL. While that sounds like it should be paired with a lethal pass rush, in practice it just means opposing teams know they should attack the blitz-happy Todd Bowles defense with a quick passing attack. The Bucs blitz 41.3% of the time, the third most in the league. Despite this, they have just six sacks (28th), 55 pressures (T-26th), and a 30.7% pressure rate (29th) this season. Pair this info together, and that tells me the Steelers and quarterback Aaron Rodgers shouldn’t feel like they have the freedom to hold onto the ball forever, but they should be able to exploit the defense if they’re smart and playing on time.

With Tampa Bay running a lot of Cover-3, the areas the Steelers should attack match well with the personnel they have available to them. Cover-3 features three deep defenders, typically a safety in the deep middle of the field, and two cornerbacks on the outside. That leaves four defenders underneath to play the flats, middle of the field, and intermediate boundary. Ways to attack this coverage include:

  • Attacking the seam (great for TEs or slot receivers)
  • Concepts like Flood, Sail, and Levels, which stress the underneath defenders by sending multiple pass catchers at them at different depths, forcing them to commit to one and creating an opening for the other
  • Slants and other quick game passing concepts that can get behind the underneath defenders quickly

While the Bucs have a decent mark in EPA/pass at -0.08 (12th), they are far worse in other metrics. They allow 6.6 yards per pass play (23rd) and struggle to stop pass catchers from creating after the catch. They’ve allowed 647 yards after the catch (29th), and +103 YAC over expectation.

Zyon McCollum, Jacob Parrish, and rookie nickel Keionte Scott are taking most of their snaps at cornerback, with Benjamin Morrison missing each of the last two games with injury. Parrish is the only CB on the team with an interception (1). McCollum is having a solid season so far, with decent marks in coverage EPA (-5.3), passer rating allowed (68.8), but he has just three career interceptions, and nearly half of his career PBUs came two seasons ago. He’s also got an absurdly high missed tackle rate (25%) this season, due largely to a poor game against Green Bay where he missed four tackles. Parrish is their most targeted defensive back (30) and has allowed 18 receptions for 236 yards, but he’s added 5 PBUs and has just one missed tackle this season. Scott, the rookie, has struggled in coverage, allowing 14 receptions on 18 targets. His missed-tackle rate is 18.5%, with one missed tackle in each game.

At safety, the Bucs will likely be without Antoine Winfield Jr. for a second straight game as he has yet to participate in practice this week while recovering from a rib injury. Ifeatu Melifonwu will be the next man up. He was only targeted twice last week, allowing one catch for 15 yards, and also adding a missed tackle. Smith, for as good as he is against the run, has been a liability against the pass, surrendering three touchdowns and an opposing passer rating of 135.3 when targeted.

Linebackers Trotter and Alex Anzalone are also gettable, as they’ve combined to allow 28 of 36 targets to be completed for 316 yards and a score. Both do have an interception, however.

Overall, this should be a winnable game for the Steelers offense. They may not find the same success on the ground as in recent weeks, but they should still feature Jaylen Warren as a pass-catching weapon out of the backfield. I’d expect a heavy dose of Pat Freiermuth, Darnell Washington, and Germie Bernard, too.

item.title: 5 things to watch as Giants face Saints in Week 6 of 2026 NFL season
item.description: Here are the main storylines to watch as the Giants look to keep the momentum going against the Saints in Week 6…
item.content:encoded:
Regardless of how Sunday's 27-27 tie against the Commanders ended, the end result was that the Giants are 3-1-1 and remain on top of the NFC East.

It was a game New York should have won, but then were lucky not to lose. It's now imperative they put that game in the rearview mirror and focus on a winnable home game against the 1-4 New Orleans Saints.

Here are the main storylines to watch as the Giants look to keep the momentum going…

Cam Skattebo looks for redemption

Skattebo has been a workhorse this season, although his statistical output could probably best be described as steady but unspectacular. 

He will have added motivation to perform in Sunday's game.

Skattebo's overtime fumble with the Giants in field goal range cost them a chance to win the Commanders game, which is obviously something he'll be looking to immediately atone for. 

In addition, he'll have last year's loss to the Saints in the back of his mind, because his costly red zone fumble in the fourth quarter was returned for an 86-yard touchdown to cost New York a potential win.

Ball security will clearly be a primary focus for Skattebo this week, but he'll also be looking to rack up plenty of yardage against the Saints' 30th ranked run defense.

Turnovers will be critical

Last Sunday's game was the first all season where the Giants haven't forced a turnover. 

They had created eight in the first four games, but this was the first time in the John Harbaugh Era that they lost the turnover battle.

The Saints' only win of the year over Baltimore was the only time this season that they had zero turnovers. 

They've turned the ball over 11 times in their four losses, including three or more in three of those games. 

That underlines how important it will be for New York to be as opportunistic as they were in earlier games.  

Will Jameis Winston keep feeding Malik Nabers?

New York had its best offensive output of the season in Washington, as they registered 408 net yards on offense.

A major part of their gameplan was to force the ball to Nabers as often as possible.

Nabers responded with his second 100-yard game in a row and a key touchdown.

Nabers had only been targeted 26 times in the first four games combined, and there is always concern that he might get frustrated over a lack of touches.

In Week 5, the Giants made more of a concerted effort to get him involved as he had 20 targets and ultimately ended up with 11 receptions.

Clearly this is something the Giants should keep doing until opposing defenses prove they can stop it.

Jermaine Eluemunor's status

Eluemunor suffered a calf injury against the Commanders, forcing the Giants into changes. Despite saying he felt a pop in his calf, the MRI scan was clean, so the veteran has apparently avoided any serious injury.

However, he may not be able to suit up for the Saints game.

Last Sunday, the Giants turned to backup Marcus Mbow to replace Eluemunor and likely would do so again this Sunday.

The potential effect on rookie guard Francis Mauigoa here should not be ignored. New York already changed the starter at center in recent weeks with Bryan Hudson replacing John Michael Schmitz, meaning Mauigoa could have players on either side of him who he is less familiar with. 

The rookie played tackle in college and general manager Joe Schoen said back in April that he could play there in the future if necessary. However, the plan for now is for him to remain on the inside rather than considering him as a potential short-term Eluemunor replacement.

Can the Giants keep Chris Olave quiet?

The most dangerous weapon on the New Orleans roster is Olave, who is well on the way to a fourth thousand-yard season in five years. In fact, he's on course for a career year as he is currently averaging over 100 receiving yards per game.

Olave is second in the NFL in catches and receiving yards, and leads the league in first downs as he has established great chemistry with quarterback Tyler Shough.

The Giants will hope to limit the damage from Olave, who was held to a season-low 46 yards on four catches in the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings last Sunday.

Although Olave is New Orleans' number one target, he only has one touchdown this season. New York therefore needs to be wary of the Saints' tight ends in the red zone as Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant have three touchdown catches each.

item.title: 5 things to watch as Jets face Patriots in Week 6 of 2026 NFL season
item.description: Here are the main storylines to watch as the Jets face the Patriots in a critical AFC East matchup in Week 6...
item.content:encoded:
The Jets avoided a fourth straight loss when they held on to beat the Cleveland Browns last Sunday.

However, if they are to keep the momentum going, they'll need to do so on the road against an old adversary, the New England Patriots.

Here are the main storylines to watch as the Jets face the defending AFC champs on the road...

The Patriots hit their stride at the worst possible time for the Jets

Three weeks into the regular season, New England was struggling badly, and Jets fans might have been looking ahead to this game as a winnable one.

However, they've reversed their fortunes in recent weeks and are now 3-2 heading into Sunday's matchup.

QB Drake Maye was an MVP contender last season, but got off to a bad start in 2026 as he had just one touchdown pass and six interceptions in the first three games.

And yet, the Patriots beat the high-powered Buffalo Bills on a late touchdown pass from Maye to Efton Chism in Week 4 before blowing out the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5.

Maye threw seven touchdowns with just one interception in those two games, as he seems to be firing on all cylinders again.

The Jets are getting some guys back

Rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr. has been activated from IR, and linebacker Kiko Mauigoa returned to practice after missing the past few games.

However, running back Breece Hall, guard Dylan Parham,and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell are still not practicing, meaning the Jets might remain without three offensive starters.

Although Braelon Allen delivered against the Browns with 116 rushing yards and the game-winning touchdown, Hall offers more in the passing game and gives the Jets a more varied rushing attack, so his return is eagerly anticipated. 

Cooper should boost a passing game that has stalled over the past two weeks.

Can the Jets keep Geno Smith upright?

A major issue that has held back the Jets' passing game is Smith seeing more pressure in the pocket.

Smith has been sacked seven times over the past two games, with the Jets averaging just 120 net passing yards.

Part of that is on Smith, who has been indecisive at times and holding onto the ball for too long.

However, he may have more confidence in and better chemistry with some of the players who have been missing, which could mean he is reluctant to get rid of the ball in certain situations.

The Pats are without their two best pass rushers from last season, as K'Lavon Chaisson departed during the offseason and Harold Landry is on the PUP list. The pair combined for 16 sacks last season.

In their absence, Elijah Ponder has stepped up with 4.5 sacks in the first five games.

Defending the deep ball 

Maye had a lot of success airing the ball out against the Raiders, as he completed four passes for longer than 30 yards, including two for touchdowns.

His 374 passing yards represented the second highest output of his career and he did this without A.J. Brown, who may be ready to return on Sunday.

That's a concern for Gang Green, who kept the Browns out of the end zone for most of last week's game but then gave up the go-ahead score with six minutes to go on a 29-yard throw from Deshaun Watson to rookie Denzel Boston.

Brandon Stephens, who had been called for a questionable pass interference penalty a few snaps earlier, was beaten on the play.

Safety Minkah Fitzpatrick can help in this regard, something that was on display against the Browns when he ranged across the field to break up a deep ball in the fourth quarter.

Can David Bailey keep this up?

In last season's win over the Browns, Will McDonald tied a team record with four sacks. However, he was unable to maintain that momentum as he went without a sack in the next five games and only had one more all season.

Star rookie David Bailey had a similar performance in his breakout game on Sunday, with his three sacks tying the Jets' single-game rookie sack record.

He will hope to be able to build on that against a New England team that could be without their blindside pass protector, Will Campbell, who was injured in last week's game.

item.title: Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams tandem a ‘pleasant surprise’ for Chiefs
item.description: Kansas City’s defensive coordinator broke down the secondary depth on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Kansas City Chiefs feature a largely retooled defense after multiple key contributors departed in free agency last offseason.

The unit currently ranks seventh in the league, allowing 19.3 points per game. Much of that falls on a secondary that features rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane — the sixth overall selection from April’s draft.

Speaking before Thursday’s practice, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo looked back on Delane’s strong game in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders and lauded the job the rookie is doing opposite second-year pro Nohl Williams.

“[Delane] is on a progression upward,” remarked the coach. “I’m a little hard on corners. I would like more. I think he would tell you that. He’s tackled really well — although there was one play against Vegas where he let it get outside. Those are the ones I remember.

“He’s coming along really good,” Spags continued. “I think him and Nohl together have been a pleasant surprise. I really didn’t know how that was going to go because you have a rookie and then you have a second-year guy. They’re playing aggressive like we want.

“There’s been some things there that we need to iron out,” Spagnuolo pointed out. “We can’t get as many penalties. There’s some leverage things. There were a couple at the end of the game that I thought Mansoor should have taken away. We talked about it. We’re going to live with some rookie mistakes and some second-year veteran mistakes. All in all, I think those guys have been pretty solid for us.”

Delane was limited in training camp due to a shoulder injury that he then aggravated in Week 1. Spagnuolo believes the rookie has the ailment out of his mind, as shown by his willingness to come up in run support.

“I think, instinctively, he wants to,” Spagnuolo observed. “He was a physical guy at LSU. We harp on that here. We guilt those guys into being physical because when they’re not, we put it on tape. And I just think that’s him, he plays that way. Whatever the shoulder and everything, I think he’s kind of put it out of his mind, which is a good thing. You want to play like that.”

Before leaving in Week 1, Delane made a spectacular interception on the play that injured his shoulder. Spagnuolo remarked on Delane’s natural ability, but the coach also had some advice for avoiding future injury.

“That was a little more of an instinctive thing,” he recalled. “The down took a little while. I think he undercut it. He has a knack for that. He undercut one at practice yesterday that he was not supposed to. So we’ve got to make sure that he does it when the coverage says that you can do that. That was a good play that he made. I told him ‘Don’t fall the ground anymore so you don’t get hurt.’”

The Chiefs have actually had two interceptions by rookie defensive backs. Undrafted safety Xavier Nwankpa — who has taken only two defensive snaps over four games — snagged a pass on the Raiders’ final drive in Week 4 to seal the win. Spagnuolo explained how a depth player, largely on the roster for special teams, made the key play.

“In that situation at the end of the game,” the coach said, “sometimes we put in a lot of DBs. He’s one of those I think seven — I forget which personnel we were in. That situation called for us putting those guys in. That’s what put him out there. If we get into that situation again, he’s part of that package. So you may see him again in there.”

As the team moves forward, Spagnuolo knows depth in the secondary matters. He is happy to have veteran Chamarri Conner back from a knee injury to round out a safety rotation with Chris Roland-Wallace, Jaden Hicks, and Alohi Gilman. He is also high on how cornerback Kristian Fulton performed in Delane’s absence and is happy to have another boundary option when needed.

“I’m glad we got back, is Chamarri,” Spagnuolo declared. “I’m sure you’ve watched the tape just like we have. Physically, I thought he played really good and had some really physical hits. Over on the sideline, he caused an incomplete pass, but I’d like to have him there more. And the guy that just seems to be a constant stabilizing guy is Chris Roland-Wallace. He’s a jack-of-all-trades for us. We can put him in at different spots.”

With Conner, a fourth-year player in the system, back in the lineup, the Chiefs will tweak the safety rotation to keep Hicks and Gilman involved.

“You can see now, so Chamarri’s back, but I think Jaden and A.G. still deserve to play. We rolled them through. I think Kristian Fulton has had some good downs. So, you see him rolling in there, and we’re going into the fifth game of the season for us. And I think the more you can do that in the first half of the season, I think the better off you’re going to be. Because somewhere along the way, we’re going to get nicked up and it’d be good for those guys to have some reps on their belt.”

item.title: Five Good Texans Questions with Big Cat Country
item.description: Gus Logue of Big Cat Country joins BRB for five questions
item.content:encoded:
Stay in this business long enough and you get to know the people on the other side. That is particularly true within the AFC South when we have these games twice a season. Gus Logue of Big Cat Country and I have been doing this for all five seasons that I have been doing five questions. The Jaguars have become the chief rival for the Texans as it pertains to the playoffs and this year is no different. This time the interdivision battle goes to London. The 4-1 Jaguars stand between the Texans and getting back into the playoff conversation. We started with the London angle.

Battle Red Blog: Jacksonville has been the unofficial home team in London for several years. Do you see that giving them key advantages on Sunday?

Gus Logue: Not really. Jacksonville was the “home” team in last week’s game against Philadelphia, but it seemed like Eagles fans outnumbered Jaguars fans 10-to-1. 

The familiarity of traveling overseas could be an edge, but really, the Jaguars’ biggest advantage this week is the simple fact that they’re already in London. The Texans still have to cross an ocean and acclimate themselves to a new continent.

After the win against the Eagles, Liam Coen said, “We really didn’t get to practice hard last week. It was one of those weird weeks, because we were a little nicked up, and then you got the travel.” I expect the Jaguars to play a cleaner game against the Texans than they did against the Eagles, even with Houston being the tougher opponent. 

BRB: It’s year two of the Travis Hunter experience. How is that going? How is the breakdown between offensive and defensive snaps looking?

GL: It is going GREAT, thank you for asking!

After playing 67% of offensive snaps and 36% of defensive snaps as a rookie, Hunter is now being deployed full-time as a starting cornerback while seeing a couple of offensive snaps per game. He had a 1st down catch on an option route last week. 

His defensive tape is highly encouraging. In the first two weeks of the season, Hunter looked really solid, but a bit hesitant coming back from the knee injury that cut his rookie season short. It didn’t take long for him to get his swagger back, because Hunter has looked like a field-tilting, quarterback-baiting, difference-making CB over the past month. 

BRB: Are there any new faces in Jacksonville that will have a dramatic impact on the outcome on Sunday?

GL: All-Pro long snapper Ross Matiscik was injured last week, so the Jaguars will be flying someone in to fill his spot (though nose tackle DaVon Hamilton filled in very admirably). 

I don’t know who Matiscik’s replacement is quite yet, but beyond that spot, keep an eye on rookie receiver Josh Cameron. He hasn’t quite out-snapped Brian Thomas Jr., but it wouldn’t be bold to say he is outplaying him. 

It’s also worth shouting out running back Bhayshul Tuten and Ventrell Miller, as they have been everything Jacksonville could’ve hoped for after letting Travis Etienne and Devin Lloyd walk in free agency. PFF has Tuten and Miller graded as the top players at their respective positions this season. 

BRB: How do you see the AFC South race shaping up? Secondarily, which divisional opponent do Jags fans enjoy beating the most?

GL: I agree with the popular take that Houston is better than their record and remains a threat to win the division. But it’s hard not to feel confident about the Jaguars, given they’ve already built a three-game lead over the Texans during the toughest part of their season. (The Colts and Titans are dog water.)

I expect Jacksonville to repeat as AFC South champs, and Houston to sneak into the playoffs as a Wild Card team. It helps that the AFC West isn’t as deep as expected. Even if the Jaguars sweep the Texans in the regular season, I will be praying to the football gods that Will Anderson Jr. does not make it far in the bracket. 

We despise the Titans. They were the only team to defeat the Jaguars during their incredible 1999 season — and they did it three times! Plus, Derrick Henry (a Jacksonville native) embarrassed us plenty of times. We hate that Peyton Manning and Andrew Luck ran the division for so long, and the current rivalry with Houston is legit a great one, but we will always enjoy beating the Titans more than any other team.

BRB: The Jags opened as 2.5 point favorites according to Fanduel. Do you see the Jags covering that? Are there any prop bets you feel comfortable recommending?

GL: I think that if this game were played out 10 times, the Jaguars would win and cover the spread in 6 or 7 of those scenarios. So I’ll pick them to cover but without much confidence. A healthy Nico Collins and a rejuvenated Marvin Harrison Jr. could cause serious issues for Jacksonville’s secondary, and we all know the threat that Houston’s defense poses against suspect offensive lines. 

Woody Marks under 47.5 rushing yards is an easy recommendation, considering Jacksonville has allowed 45 rushing yards total over the past two weeks. They join the 1969 Dallas Cowboys as the only Super Bowl-era teams to not allow an opposing player to rush for 40+ yards in their first five games of a season. We really think Marks is gonna be the first? I do expect big performances from C.J. Stroud and Jaguars tight end Brenton Strange (over 37.5 receiving yards looks nice). 

Score prediction: Jaguars 20, Texans 16.

We want to thank Gus so much for his time an attention to this feature. These interchanges are always interesting because the people involved are always so nice and accommodating even when the games themselves are tense. We want to wish Gus and the Jaguars the best of luck for the rest of the season. As per usual, we hope that the luck begins on Monday morning.

item.title: Bills news: Joe Brady issues warning to James Cook about fumbles.
item.description: James Cook is a talented RB with a fumbling problem. If he doesn’t improve, Joe Brady says he will reduce his touches.
item.content:encoded:
James Cook has blossomed into one of the best running backs in the NFL, including serving as the league’s rushing leader during the 2025 campaign. But Cook has been plagued with a case of the fumbles since the start of the 2025 season, a problem that is once again rearing its ugly head early in 2026.

While the Buffalo Bills (4-1) were able to overcome a pair of costly Cook fumbles in last week’s primetime win over the Los Angeles Rams, Cook needs to get better at taking care of the football, a point that his head coach reiterated several times this week during sessions with the media.

Heading into a Week 6 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders, Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks leads off by examining Cook’s fumbling issue, including why Brady said Cook could see his workload reduced if he doesn’t find a way to hang onto the football.

Check out the news items below and then let us know your thoughts on Cook’s issues with ball security in the comments section.

Joe Brady issues warning to James Cook

Last season, while leading all running backs in rushing yards with 1,621 yards, James Cook managed to cough up the football a league-high six times (seven if you include the playoffs). Through the first five games of this year, Cook has already fumbled the football four times, which gives him 11 fumbles in just 24 games dating back to the beginning of the 2025 season.

What’s most troubling about Cook’s fumbling is it appears to be a recent problem. Cook fumbled just six times over his first 750 touches during his first three seasons (playoffs included), which equates to one fumble for every 125 carries/touches. Since the start of last year, Cook has given the ball away 11 times over 487 touches, once every 44 times he has the ball in his hands.

After being pressed on the issue a few times earlier in the week, Brady admitted that as talented as Cook is, and as dangerous of a weapon he is for Buffalo’s offense, something has got to change with the fumbles.

“That can’t happen, and it’s going to cost us football games,” Brady said Tuesday, “and it almost cost us (Monday night). We can’t confuse that because we won the game. That’s OK. “It’s got to improve, or the carries are going to decrease.”

Despite the fumbles, Brady knows exactly how valuable Cook is to this offense—he’s clearly the second most talented player behind Josh Allen—and Brady stands by his bell cow back, even after the ball security issues.

“He’s doing so many good things running the football, and I don’t want to lose sight of how great he’s running the ball right now,” Brady said. “But we’re putting the ball on the ground, and it’s negating all the positive.”

For his part, Cook accepts full responsibility for his fumbles and knows he needs to figure out this issue, and fast.

“It could of just changed the game,” Cook said. “Just gotta hold onto it and just work on it each and every day. … Just need to take more care of the ball and hold myself accountable.”

If Cook’s carries do decrease, former fourth-round pick Ray Davis would appear to be the most likely candidate to receive those touches.
